Deal summary: Lost to self-hosted stack. Marigold chose vLLM/TGI + TensorRT-LLM path to run on existing DGX fleet for latency-sensitive reranking. Main drivers: predictable token cost, kernel-level control, and ability to patch weights internally.

Recent timeline (CRM-style):
- 2024-09-10: Lead created after webinar. Intro email from Jordan; asked for low-p95 SLA guidance.
- 2024-09-25: Discovery call (Jordan, LucIa) - workload detail: 50ms target p95 for reranker @ 180 qps; embeddings batch jobs overnight.
- 2024-10-12: Security questionnaire submitted; request for KMS integration and audit log retention (2 years).
- 2024-11-19: Perf deep-dive (ff_2024-11-19_8741) with infra/SRE; discussed KV cache, model sharding, cold-start mitigation.
- 2024-12-02: Pricing & TCO workshop. Marigold ran 3-year TCO comparing Redwood Dedicated vs in-house amortized A100 fleet.
- 2025-01-07: Procurement pause: CFO flagged CAPEX preference; asked infra to prototype vLLM/TGI.
- 2025-02-12: Final decision: procurement signed off on self-host approach using vLLM and TensorRT-LLM in prod. No vendor contract executed.

Key requirements captured: 
- Latency: strict sub-60ms p95 for reranker at steady 150-200 qps.
- Throughput: burst to 400qps during peak auctions.
- SW/HW: A100/DGX class hardware, desire for TRT kernels in production.
- Controls: full code/weights access, air-gapped test lanes for compliance.

Why they moved away from Redwood (quoting notes):
- "Unit economics get better once we amortize HW; we can control batching and kernel choices ourselves."
- "Compliance team insisted on code-level visibility and the ability to run air-gapped tests."
- No strong internal champion to push an externally managed vendor through procurement.
